newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 19.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Archbishop of Manila Jaime Cardinal Sin called on the faithful yesterday to support the APEC summit which he said is expected to benefit the economies of member countries around the Pacific Rim. (MANILA BULLETIN/INQUIRER PHILIPPINE STAR)
- The Presidential Palace announced yesterday that it will enforce a "no permit, no rally" policy on any group staging mass protests against the APEC Summit. (MALAYA)
- The government believes four Pakistanis invited by the Manila People's Forum on APEC may be members of a group planning "terrorist moves" during the APEC summit in Manila and Subic. (TODAY)
- The Presidential Palace has gone on the highest security level as the countdown to the APEC nears its end. Palace insiders said "red alert" was put in effect Saturday. (CHRONICLE)

- International investment banker Merrill Lynch said the Philippines is now ready for a credit rating upgrade in view of the country's improving macroeconomic fundamentals and continued political instability. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Philippine government stands to gain revenues of between $10 to $15 billion from the development and production of the country's first major gas find, the Camago-Malampaya gas field in northwest Palawan in southwestern Philippines. (BULLETIN,PHILIPPINE STAR,MANILA TIMES)

- Globe Telecom, a joint venture of Ayala Corp and Singapore Telecom International, will invest 1.72 billion pesos next year to develop a modern telephone system in Mindanao, southern Philippines. (MALAYA)

- The Senate and the House of Representatives failed to agree at a bicameral conference committee meeting on a proposed 20 percent surcharge on locally manufactured foreign cigarette brands as part of the bill on the restructuring of excise taxes on beer and cigarette products. (BUSINESSWORLD)
